reading.body:
H.R. 7110 has 17 recorded sponsors and cosponsors, all Democrats, and no lobbying filing from 2025 or later names it.

The support is entirely one-party. Summer Lee sponsors, and the 16 cosponsors run from Eleanor Norton and Rashida Tlaib to Bennie Thompson, Andre Carson and Frederica Wilson. A bill with no cross-party cosponsor and no recorded vote in the data is a statement of position, not a measure with a path through the House.

The bill's own text tags it to bias and civil rights. That places it in the governance layer of AI, the rules written about how systems decide, rather than in the compute, buildings and power layer where capacity is actually built. The two are not unrelated, since compliance obligations fall on whoever operates the models, but nothing in this data connects the bill to a data center, a grid interconnection or a power contract.

What the data does not cover is large. It gives no vote counts, no committee action, no hearing, no text of the provisions, and no indication of what the bill would require or of whom. The lobbying count is the most informative absence: zero filings for 2025 or later name H.R. 7110, which means no registered lobbyist has reported it as an issue in that period. That is a fact about disclosure, not about industry sentiment, because a filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue, and a filing that omits it shows only that no one reported it.

summary: H.R. 7110, Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-01-15. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: bias and civil rights. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
